extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO discipline, and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 describing the procedural requirements for notice, respondent's opportunity to contest, grounds to avoid identical discipline, publication/notice obligations, and the statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose reciprocal discipline (e.g., public reprimand) based on a state disciplinary decision; the OED Director filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' informs the respondent of the Complaint and the request for identical discipline and directs that if the respondent seeks to contest imposition of identical discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the respondent must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information the respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d). Failure to respond may result in imposition of the requested discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical violation identified: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation found of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) is applied where the practitioner 'has been publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.' The Final Order here states the respondent violated § 10.23(b)(6) by having been publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a duly constituted state authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden to show a genuine issue under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent who wishes to contest imposition of identical discipline must file within 40 days a response containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based on grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order directed the respondent to provide all information to establish a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d); the Final Order states that respondent did not file such a response and therefore 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and ... a public reprimand of Respondent is appropriate.' (Emphasizes procedural default consequences.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: Following imposition of public discipline, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs that the OED Director shall publish the Final Order; publish a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette; and, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, give notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public. Disciplinary decisions are posted in the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for action: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation of statutory authority supporting the USPTO's power to impose and publish disciplinary actions; included as legal basis in the Notice of Reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Reprimand content requirements (template/example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Reprimand must identify the practitioner (name, city, registration number), state the disciplinary violation (e.g., violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by being publicly reprimanded on ethical grounds by a state authority), summarize the state decision (cite the decision), describe the underlying misconduct (e.g., criminal conviction and nature of the crime), and cite the USPTO statutory/regulatory authority for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording in this document: includes practitioner's name and registration number, states the reason for public reprimand, cites the state appellate decision (In the Matter of Lawrence Ira Wechsler, 66 A.D.3d 277, 886 N.Y.S.2d 35 (2009)), describes the criminal conviction (plea of guilty to two counts of failing to file a New York State tax return, citation to state tax law and People v. Lawrence Wechsler docket), and lists the statutory/regulatory citations (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D); 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59). Also directs where disciplinary decisions are posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely respond results in default determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file the required response within the 40-day period specified by the Notice and Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the Director may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that imposition of the requested discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'Respondent has not filed a response to the Notice and Order. 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Accordingly, it is hereby determined that: 1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and 2) a public reprimand of Respondent is appropriate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Service procedure for Final Order (certificate of service)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service: mailing the Final Order by first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent (or their counsel) and providing the mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in the document shows mailing to counsel at a specified address with date; this evidences the required service/notice mechanics for disciplinary orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary grounds illustrated: criminal conviction and conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A conviction of a serious crime and engaging in conduct that reflects adversely on a practitioner's fitness to practice can form the basis for public censure/reprimand by a state authority and reciprocal discipline by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This case's factual basis: the New York Appellate Division publicly censured the respondent for being convicted of a serious crime and for engaging in conduct reflecting adversely on his fitness to practice; the criminal conviction was based on a guilty plea to two counts of failing to file a New York State tax return (New York State Tax Law § 1801(a)), for tax years 2003 and 2004 (People v. Lawrence Wechsler, Docket No. 07-178854). Such factual findings are sufficient to trigger the disciplinary process under the cited regulations.
